Taxonomy:
1. Subgraph-centric multi-hop KGQA (root)
   1.1 Inference-time subgraph retrieval & prompting (SG-RAG MOT, GraphTrace, arxiv:2202.13296) — note SR is trainable retriever + reasoner.
   1.2 Training-signal / supervision design for multi-hop
       1.2.1 Intermediate-step supervision (arxiv:2101.03737)
       1.2.2 Context-augmented supervision (arxiv:2609.12230, and to a degree arxiv:2406.09994)
   1.3 Architecture-centric relational reasoning (DSSAGN doi:10.3390/electronics13081436, arxiv:2202.13296 NSM-based)
   1.4 RL-based KG reasoning (doi:10.1016/j.knosys.2023.110760) and repaired-RL in arxiv:2609.12230
2. Knowledge-context supply in multimodal QA (arxiv:2406.09994) — could be a separate category (context quantity in KBVQA).
3. Domain-specific KG construction & QA generation (arxiv:2609.12230 GraphMERT) — maybe subcategory.

- more relevant context improves reasoning (but bounds exist)

common_datasets: WebQSP, CWQ, MetaQA, Freebase, KVQA/CRIC-VQA/FVQA (multimodal), disease-specific KGs (Gastroparesis, Diabetes), COVID-19 economic KG.

common_benchmarks: WebQSP, CWQ, MetaQA.

common_metrics: Hits@1, answer accuracy/EM, answer coverage rate; MCQ accuracy; option-shuffling robustness.

repeated_limitations (with paper ids):
- Context/subgraph size trade-off: larger context adds noise (arxiv:2202.13296, arxiv:2406.09994)
- No repair/data-cleaning in retrieval/prompting methods (SG-RAG, GraphTrace, arxiv:2202.13296)
- Limited/no standard-benchmark generalization (arxiv:2609.12230 disease-specific; GraphTrace domain-specific; DSSAGN no numbers)

- Context-augmented LLM SFT evaluated on standard benchmarks (WebQSP/CWQ/MetaQA) rather than only synthetic domain MCQ
- Matched-token/matched-context-size control isolating passage locality from supervision volume
- Context-size/precision sweep (inverted-U test) in LLM KGQA supervision
- Component-wise ablation (context vs repair vs RL) with untouched held-out test sets and seeds
- Cross-domain transfer: context supervision trained on one corpus evaluated on another
- Combining intermediate-step supervision with context-triple supervision
- Repair loop applied to retrieved context (GraphRAG) rather than KG extraction

contradictions:
- arxiv:2406.09994 "excess distracts" vs the assumption that more context helps; and arxiv:2202.13296 shows larger subgraphs add noise and reduce Hits@1. Contradicts monotonic benefit assumed by the idea (H1/H4).
- arxiv:2609.12230 reports 100% on cleaned retained one-hop validation (repair works) — while this is claimed as factual grounding; potential artifact. Maybe phrase as tension rather than contradiction between papers.
- SG-RAG MOT says merging "up to some point" helps — again inverted-U vs more context.

input.field_name: Multi-hop knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) with subgraph/context supervision and LLM fine-tuning
input.idea_position: The idea sits in the 'Context-augmented triple supervision' leaf under 'Supervision-signal design for multi-hop training', and additionally spans the sibling leaf 'Adaptive repair / data-cleaning loops' and the RL branch 'RL-based KG reasoning and lower-hop RL transfer'. Its closest neighbor, arxiv:2609.12230, occupies the same three leaves simultaneously with method and evaluation overlap ~1.0/0.9, making the idea's intended position already populated rather than adjacent to it; the subgraph-context framing it shares with 'Subgraph-centric reasoning' is where it connects to the broader field, and arxiv:2406.09994 supplies the only contextual-quantity evidence (from multimodal QA) that bears on the idea's context-volume assumption.

repeated_limitations.description: Context/subgraph size is a trade-off: too small excludes the answer, too large introduces noise that degrades QA (arxiv:2202.13296); supplying a fixed larger number of triples is worse than a dynamic, question-fitted number, and the work title explicitly frames excess context as distracting (arxiv:2406.09994). This directly qualifies the idea's assumption that same-passage context helps.

Retrieval/prompting methods (GraphRAG-style) perform no training, no supervision-design comparison, no data repair, and no RL, leaving the training-side questions open (SG-RAG MOT, GraphTrace, arxiv:2202.13296).

Evaluation is domain-specific and/or synthetic rather than on established public benchmarks, limiting external validity (disease-specific KGs in arxiv:2609.12230; COVID-19 economic KG in GraphTrace; synthetic QA items per arxiv:2609.12230 Section 6).

Claims are unverifiable from the retrieved artifact: DSSAGN reports no datasets, baselines, metrics or numbers in its abstract, and the path-based adversarial RL record has neither abstract nor accessible full text.

The evaluation set is modified by the method being evaluated: adaptive repair removes/quarantines triples and refreshes the validation set, after which models reach 100% on the 'cleaned retained' one-hop set (arxiv:2609.12230), creating a selection/cleaning confound.

No public code or data release could be found for the closest and most complex method (arxiv:2609.12230) or for GraphMERT, whereas the simpler subgraph-retrieval and intermediate-supervision baselines do release code (arxiv:2202.13296, arxiv:2101.03737).

underexplored_combinations: Context-augmented LLM supervision evaluated on standard public benchmarks (WebQSP/CWQ/MetaQA) instead of only synthetic domain MCQ — but note this requires text-grounded KGs with passage provenance that Freebase-based benchmarks lack.

Matched-token / matched-context-size controls that isolate passage localization from raw supervision volume, plus a context-size sweep to test the inverted-U (precision vs excess) in LLM KGQA supervision.
A component-wise decomposition (context vs repair vs RL) with an untouched, never-edited held-out test set and seed-level variance reporting.

Combining intermediate-step supervision (arxiv:2101.03737) with context-triple supervision (arxiv:2609.12230), which are alternative answers to the same missing-signal problem and have not been compared.
Applying the repair loop to retrieved/prompted context (GraphRAG pipelines: SG-RAG MOT, GraphTrace) rather than only to KG-extraction triples.
Cross-corpus transfer of context-augmented supervision (train on one text corpus/KG, test on another) to test whether the mechanism is domain-general.

contradictions.description: The idea's H1/H4 assume more same-passage context is (at least weakly) beneficial, but retrieved work in adjacent settings reports the opposite direction at high context volume: arxiv:2406.09994 is framed as 'Precision Empowers, Excess Distracts' and shows dynamic (question-fitted) triples beat fixed larger amounts, while arxiv:2202.13296 shows larger subgraphs introduce noise and reduce QA Hits@1 even as answer coverage rises. SG-RAG MOT likewise finds merging helps 'up to some point'.

arxiv:2609.12230 claims the repair stage yields 100% accuracy on the cleaned retained one-hop validation sets, presenting this as a strengthened factual foundation; because the same loop quarantines triples and refreshes the validation set, this claim is in tension with the standard requirement that evaluation data be independent of the method — accuracy gains and evaluation-set editing are not separable as reported.

Two distinct remedies are offered for the same 'missing multi-hop supervision' problem without being compared: learned intermediate-step supervision for an embedding state machine (arxiv:2101.03737) versus passage-local context triples for LLM SFT (arxiv:2609.12230). Which added signal (intermediate reasoning distributions vs surrounding factual context) drives multi-hop gains is unresolved.

input.description: The idea's mechanism requires each target triple to be traceable to a source passage so that same-passage supporting triples can be attached (as arxiv:2609.12230 does via GraphMERT source-chunk identifiers). Standard multi-hop KGQA benchmarks (WebQSP, CWQ, MetaQA) are built over KGs (Freebase, a movies KG) whose triples are not shipped with source-passage provenance, so passage-local context graphs cannot be constructed for them without an external corpus. This means the natural external-validity test (does the effect hold on standard benchmarks?) may be infeasible as stated, and generalization would require text-grounded KGs instead. The landscape's underexplored combination of 'context supervision on standard benchmarks' therefore may not be achievable with the idea's exact mechanism.
input.question: Can passage-local context-triple supervision be constructed at all for standard multi-hop KGQA benchmarks, or does the mechanism require text-grounded KGs with passage provenance (making generalization a different, harder question)?
input.rationale: This affects the design of any experiment intended to test generalizability and thus which re-scoped contribution is feasible; it also constrains the choice of benchmark and the comparison to arxiv:2609.12230. It was surfaced by the landscape mapping and has not been investigated.

The landscape also records the field's dominant approaches, shared datasets/benchmarks/metrics (WebQSP, CWQ, MetaQA; Hits@1/EM), six repeated limitations, six underexplored combinations, and three contradictions — chiefly that "excess distracts" evidence (arxiv:2406.09994, arxiv:2202.13296, SG-RAG MOT) contradicts the idea's monotonic-context assumption, and that arxiv:2609.12230's 100%-on-cleaned-retained-set claim is entangled with its own evaluation-set editing; I added U010, that standard Freebase-based benchmarks lack the source-passage provenance the mechanism needs.
